Round 311 — current CPU decode critical path and next controlled model discriminator
Date: 2026-10-13 (JST)
Status: read-only source/evidence research. No test, benchmark, build, inference, model/server request, GPU, process or profiler action, Git operation, cleanup, or source edit. No active Main measurement record/log was opened. Main's in-flight work remains the owner of the next fresh 32K+ model sample.

## Finding

The strongest source-grounded decode candidate on the target is the existing opt-in paired IQ3_S Gate/Up AVX2 NT1 implementation, but only if a *closed* production route census confirms a material number of CPU jobs with GU type 21 and NT=1. It reuses the same quantized activation block across Gate and Up while preserving their independent weight decodes. It has an existing exact-geometry CPU parity fixture, but no retained completed parity result, spill/assembly inspection, candidate component timing, or matched model result was found in R294/R293/R250. Therefore it is a candidate for one controlled ON/OFF model axis, not an optimization or default recommendation.

Do not launch that comparison during Main's current request. After the owner closes the current 32K baseline, the smallest high-information sequence is: (1) use the closed request's route census to count `(layer, CPU ownership, GU type, NT)` and gate on type21/NT1 service; (2) run the existing paired-GU correctness fixture and inspect the produced code for spills in the exact WN/CPU build; (3) if both pass, compare switch unset versus `STRATA_IQ256_PAIRED_GU=1` in alternating fresh processes on a 32,768-token prompt plus 128 generated tokens, preserving binary/source, actual input IDs, state/cache/profile, pool worker/task setting, prefetch/gather settings, PCIe fraction/mode, MTP/draft and all output/fault checks. Compare GU phase and complete clean request wall separately. Do not use a route count from a prefill/H2D trace as a CPU decode denominator.

## What can be measured now, and ceilings

The parent supplied a qualified 32K serial official-model aggregate of 376.419 prefill tok/s and 8.2658 decode tok/s across three samples. The reciprocal of the decode rate is 120.98 ms per emitted token averaged over that tested decode segment. This is an end-to-end wall average; it includes verification/window acceptance, attention, CPU/GPU expert work, dispatch, commit and other request costs. It is not a CPU time measurement. Those aggregate figures do not expose the current IQ3_S CPU service fraction and cannot support an Amdahl bound for a CPU kernel change.

R270's source audit says existing `--stats` shows broad verifier/dispatch time and CPU-pool GU, intermediate quantization and Down phase elapsed totals, but the `pool multi` counters are pool-lifetime totals divided by rounds, can include qualifying prompt work, and include scheduling/barrier costs. They are not worker CPU time; adding nested timer spans double-counts. The existing output also lacks per-layer `(format, NT, CPU job count)` for the prompt path. Thus no reliable current phase share, memory-controller bandwidth, worker imbalance, cache-miss ceiling, or theoretical speedup fraction was found. For an eventual GU fraction `f` and measured isolated GU factor `g`, the Amdahl ceiling would be `1 / ((1-f) + f/g)`; neither `f` nor `g` is presently measured for the active candidate. Do not infer either from packed bytes or synthetic one-thread row timings.

There is a useful *source-level traffic bound*: for one type21 expert at H=2560/FF=640, each Q8_K activation is ten 292-byte blocks (2,920 B). The separate Gate and Up row traversals logically load 2 × 640 × 2,920 = 3,737,600 B per NT1 expert; the paired loop logically loads 1,868,800 B, saving 1,868,800 B of repeated activation loads/instructions. Weight payload (1,408,000 B for the two IQ3_S matrices) and both matrix decodes remain. Because the activation footprint is only 2.9 KB and Zen 3 has small private L1D, the saved requests may mostly be L1 hits; this is not a DRAM-byte saving or predicted wall-time gain. The measured/validated source must decide whether it reduces load-port pressure or instead causes spills.

## Exact route and candidate source

Reviewed combined source is under `/home/yayoi/ghq/github.com/yqYo1/Strata/.worktree/perf-native-copy-cohorts-qualified-20261012`; reviewed file content matches the curated `sync-latest-updates-20261012` copy for the relevant `iq_avx2.cpp`. SHA-256 values in the reviewed copy:

- `src/kernels/cpu/iq_avx2.cpp`: `09722bf282c5f7b4c928aa8d63fe5f2489833301564968d5240e35e29ab76b30`
- `src/kernels/cpu/native_expert.cpp`: `39c7b9e66c52edb7b42d5dd65e5c317bf322e23f1ab24f6b300640abffc989d3`
- `src/kernels/cpu/pool.cpp`: `c114539980d496ea69c17fee2ddaf1b7229668afe07586142f572d96cb8a7036`
- `src/core/expert_source.cpp`: `178c6d87f9f71e783526efd6bbd4ebd555a6986d94ffb16b26b852c06e24be3b`

At these source identities, the exact guard in `iq_avx2.cpp:477-486` is IQ3_S type 21, `nt == 1`, `n == 2560`, row width 1,100 bytes, `up_off == 640 * 1,100`, and rows in `0..640`; it selects scalar or gathered decode. `:517-525` enables it only when `STRATA_IQ256_PAIRED_GU` equals exactly `1`; default is OFF. The exact fixture is `tests/core/iq3s_paired_gu_test.cpp`, registered at `CMakeLists.txt:894-898`; it uses the production Q8_K quantizer and synthetic valid IQ3_S rows, compares output float bits across all 640 rows and partition ranges, and checks rejected geometry leaves outputs unchanged. Source presence is not a test pass and synthetic rows are not model-output correctness.

`native_expert.cpp:94-142` on AVX2 without AVX-512 selects the multirow GU kernel down to NT1 by default for eligible formats, including IQ3_S, unless flags override it. `:157-175` dispatches IQ4_NL Down separately. `pool.cpp:470-503` measures host elapsed GU, activation quantization and Down phases; `expert_source.cpp:1788-1885` builds per-window route/provider plans before pool service. Thus a pooled aggregate or a model-level `decode tok/s` cannot be credited to paired GU without its type/NT denominator and a matched phase measurement.

## Evidence trail and non-duplicate decision

- R293 (`research-native-iq3s-decode-cpu-memory-scheduling-round293-v1.txt`) identified this same exact-geometry candidate and required a live CPU `(type, NT, jobs)` census; no new denominator or service measurement was available. It specifically says activation quantization and duplicate-route grouping already exist, and says not to rerun Main's worker/task controls here.
- R294 (`research-paired-gu-prior-evidence-and-current-route-round294-v1.txt`) confirms default-off status, but its reported type-21 layer-format counts came from a four-chunk prefill H2D receipt, not CPU-owned decode. It found no exact CPU type21/NT1 job count, no bit-parity pass, no assembly/spill finding and no model timing for this flag. The existing fixture source was described but not executed.
- R250 (`research-existing-iq3s-avx2-kernel-measurement-consumers-round250-v1.txt`) found no retained exact current-WN IQ3_S/IQ4_NL AVX2 benchmark sample table; older IQ4_NL Down calibration and Intel P-core gather numbers are different formats/shapes or CPUs, not evidence for the 5600X.
- R270 (`research-decode-cpu-pool-criticalpath-candidates-round270-v1.txt`) owns pool worker/task tuning and explains why current aggregate counters cannot isolate worker busy time or add to wall. Do not repeat its worker/task matrix.
- R309 (`research-xe-b9-decode-port-candidates-round309-v1.txt`) shows no newly ported b9 IQ3_S/IQ4_NL CPU row algorithm and excludes b9 fused hit/combine from a one-token route. That is consistent with evaluating the existing paired flag rather than importing an unrelated kernel.

The current exact CPU route service and savings remain unverified. If the closed census has no or negligible type21/NT1 CPU GU jobs, stop this candidate and use that same closed sample's dominant measured phase to select a different single-axis experiment. Do not assume that 5600X's architecture implies a particular dispatch: record the parity executable's CPUID/feature output for the actual build. AMD's product page lists the 5600X as six-core and 32-MiB L3; AMD's EPYC 7003 Zen 3 guide describes 32-KB L1 and private L2 per core, useful architectural context but not target-specific cache counters or perf evidence.

## External primary sources

- AMD, [Ryzen 5 5600X product specifications](https://www.amd.com/en/products/processors/desktops/ryzen/5000-series/amd-ryzen-5-5600x.html): target core/cache SKU facts only.
- AMD, [EPYC 7003 HPC tuning guide](https://www.amd.com/content/dam/amd/en/documents/epyc-technical-docs/tuning-guides/high-performance-computing-tuning-guide-amd-epyc7003-series-processors.pdf): Zen 3 cache/core organization; this is same Zen 3 family, but a server SKU and not a 5600X timing source.
- ggml-org, [llama.cpp server CPU MoE options](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/tools/server/README.md): official `--cpu-moe`/`--n-cpu-moe` availability. This confirms a neighboring engine has an explicit CPU expert placement control, not a directly comparable packed format, pool policy, or Ryzen speedup.
- KTransformers, [AMX kernel design](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/ktransformers/blob/main/doc/en/AMX.md): primary implementation context for grouped expert work and activation sharing. It uses transformed weights and AMX-class CPUs; it motivates careful task/cache measurement but its performance claims do not transfer to Strata's IQ3_S/AVX2 path.

No CUDA/HIP inference optimization was used as evidence. No performance result, implementation recommendation for default behavior, or target-specific CPU bandwidth/cache ceiling is asserted.
